📋 Utilization review (medical-necessity decision support)

Paste a full course of care and MLS will assess whether the number of visits, frequency, and treatments look medically necessary and reasonable. Works on the pasted text — no current visit needed.

📋 Utilization review result

⚠️ Clinical decision-support only — NOT an official utilization-review determination. An authorized reviewer / medical director makes the actual determination under the applicable guidelines and payer policy.

🧾 Superbill (dx + CPT for billing)

⚠️ Suggested codes for provider review. The final Athena confirmation adds only the frozen E/M and CPT/HCPCS codes shown there; diagnoses, modifiers, units and diagnosis links stay manual. No claim is submitted.

💲 Cost estimate (MLS Good Faith Estimate)

Estimated out-of-pocket for the ordered procedure, based on the benefit information entered for this patient's plan.

⚠️ Estimate based on the benefit information entered for this patient's plan and ballpark allowed amounts — NOT a guarantee. Actual cost depends on the payer's adjudication and your contracted rates. For a verified amount, real-time insurance eligibility is required.

🎯 MIPS quality check

Advisory review of common pain/PM&R quality measures based only on this note. For any gap, a one-line snippet you could add to capture the measure.

📝 Patient handout

Plain-language home-exercise & care sheet for the current diagnosis. Edit before printing — general guidance only.

🔌 FHIR export (R4 Bundle)

A minimal FHIR R4 collection Bundle (Encounter + one Condition per ICD-10 + DocumentReference for the note). Patient identifiers are [PATIENT_ID] placeholders — no fabricated IDs.

🚩 Red-flag safety scan (advisory)

Screens the note/transcript for spine, neuro & pain red flags. Advisory only — based solely on what is documented; it never invents findings. Use clinical judgment.

🔍 Differential considerations (for the provider)

A ranked differential with rationale and what would confirm/exclude each. These are considerations for the provider, not a diagnosis.

🦴 Surgical planning (auto — for the provider)

Auto-assembled when surgery is discussed: conservative-care gaps for prior-auth, imaging concordance, surgical options, pre-op workup, and informed-consent talking points. Advisory — based only on what is documented.

💊 Opioid MME calculator (CDC morphine-milligram-equivalents)

Add the patient's opioids to compute total daily MME with CDC risk banding. Client-side math; methadone and fentanyl factors are approximate. Saved with the visit.

💉 Injection procedure note (spine / pain)

Build a structured procedure note. Pulls the indication from the current diagnosis; bracket anything not yet documented.

💵 Estimated reimbursement: —
Estimate only — ballpark national Medicare-ish averages. Actual reimbursement varies by payer, contract, geography, and modifiers.

MLS Copilot

Copilot reads a private snapshot of your own data — your panel, schedule, current visit, and the verified visit timeline for the patient you have open. Historical answers cite their source records. It suggests; you decide. Not a substitute for clinical judgment.

Runs in a secure sandbox; your saved creations stay here.

📝 Note defaults

Defaults applied to new notes. The note style is shared with MLS as a writing preference.

When this patient already has a saved, finished note in their chart, MLS seeds today's draft from it: the same section layout, plus their stable history — past medical, past surgical, family and social history, and allergies — copied forward word for word and marked “carried from last visit - review” so you can always see it was not written today.
Today's HPI, ROS, exam, assessment and plan are always written from today's visit alone, and medication doses, strengths, frequencies and routes are never carried forward — you document medications fresh every visit.
On SOAP and APSO the carried history appears after the note's sections, clearly marked, never inside them — and the copy MLS sends to athenaOne always stays exactly the five SOAP sections. You can switch it off for a single visit from the visit screen.

Tip: your standing follow-up interval lives below under Provider preferences.

🎚️ AI personalization

Standing instructions and defaults MLS applies to every note it writes for you.

Premium notes run on a priority lane for lower latency. GPT-5 mini is the newest and strongest for most notes, GPT-4o is a proven balanced choice, and GPT-4o mini is the quickest. Standard always uses GPT-4o mini.

Add reusable style/content rules and MLS follows them on every note. These are remembered instructions applied to the AI — not patient details.
e.g. Use APSO format · Keep HPI to 3 sentences · Always add return precautions · Never suggest benzodiazepines · Use my normal-exam template

Your standing comment is dropped into the Comment box on every new visit and woven into the generated note. Edit it per visit as needed.
e.g. Risk/benefit discussed; patient verbalized understanding. Follow up in 2 weeks or sooner if symptoms worsen.

Setting up MLS Assist on this computer

Four steps, once per computer. Your practice IT can do this for you; the illustrated version is at mlsscribe.com/get-extension. If a pull ever looks stuck afterwards, open the same chrome://extensions page and press ↻ on the MLS Assist card.

  1. Download the .zip and unzip it. Open chrome://extensions and turn on Developer mode (top-right).
  2. Click Load unpacked and pick the unzipped mls-assist-extension folder. (To update later, replace the folder and click ↻ Reload.)
  3. Make sure you're signed in to MLS in a tab — the extension uses that login automatically. No key to paste.
  4. On your EMR, click the 🩺 badge (bottom-right) → Dictate or select text → ✨ Generate → Insert, or run Autopilot.
🕰️ Visit notes still filling in

When a pull cannot finish reading a day's visit notes — usually because athenaOne was slow — MLS keeps the rest and reads them quietly in the background, one at a time, only while you are not using this computer. It pauses the moment you touch anything and picks up again after 20 seconds of quiet. It never brings athenaOne to the front.

Nothing waiting.
Connecting another system to MLS

Only if another program in your practice needs to read or write MLS records on its own — a billing system, a scheduler, or a second computer that will not be signed in to MLS. Most practices never need this.

Use this for the FHIR API or to authenticate the extension on a machine where you won't be signed in to MLS.

Reference for whoever sets that up: the hosted API documentation.

📥 Bringing patients in from another system

Bring many patients and their visit history across in one go. Paste your old system’s export into the box below; whoever produces that export needs it in this form: {"patients":[{"name":"Jane Doe","dob":"1980-05-01","mrn":"12345","history":[{"date":"2026-03-10","note":"..."}]}]}. Everything imported is stored encrypted, exactly like a chart created here.

🧹 EMR page text found in stored notes

Some early chart pulls captured the EMR's own page along with the note — its menus, its refresh prompt, and the script the page runs. MLS took that text back out of the stored notes and kept the untouched original beside each one. Nothing was deleted.

📥 Pull a patient from my EMR

With MLS Assist installed, open a patient in your EMR (another tab), then click below — MLS reads that chart and pulls the patient + prior visits in here. No copy-paste.

Another scheduling system can read and write this practice’s appointments over a small FHIR R4 API. Bookings made through MLS show up there; appointments it creates land on the MLS board. The whole loop:

  1. A patient books on your public booking.html?token=… page or submits the MLS patient intake — the appointment (and chart, when linked) now exists in MLS.
  2. The other scheduler polls GET /fhir/Appointment?_lastUpdated=gt<last sync> — or receives the signed webhook the moment it happens.
  3. It shows the visit as if it were booked natively, deduping by the urn:mls:appointment-id identifier. Writing back works the same way: POST /fhir/Appointment with your own identifier[] is idempotent — a retry returns the existing appointment, never a duplicate.

📣 Webhooks — push instead of poll

MLS POSTs {"event","resource"} to your https endpoint on appointment.created / updated / confirmed / cancelled / deleted, signed with HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body in the X-MLS-Signature header (sha256=<hex>). The signing secret is shown once, when the hook is added.

Verify a delivery (Node): crypto.createHmac('sha256',secret).update(rawBody).digest('hex') === req.get('X-MLS-Signature').slice(7)

Examples & field mapping

Read a week, plus everything changed since your last sync (gt is strict on whole-second UTC timestamps, so poll with the newest meta.lastUpdated you have stored):

curl -H "Authorization: Bearer mls_YOUR_KEY" \
  "https://scrivara-backend.onrender.com/fhir/Appointment?date=ge2026-07-28&date=le2026-08-04&_lastUpdated=gt2026-07-28T00:00:00Z&_count=100"

Create (idempotent — retrying with the same identifier[] returns 200 with the existing appointment, not a duplicate):

curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer mls_YOUR_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"resourceType":"Appointment","status":"booked",
       "start":"2026-08-03T14:00:00Z","end":"2026-08-03T14:30:00Z",
       "identifier":[{"system":"urn:yourscheduler:appt","value":"A-1042"}],
       "description":"New patient visit"}' \
  "https://scrivara-backend.onrender.com/fhir/Appointment"

A webhook delivery is the same shape in reverse: MLS POSTs {"event":"appointment.created","resource":{…}} to your endpoint with the header X-MLS-Signature: sha256=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body>.

Schedule and chart-history pulls are clinician-started. Today/Calendar can read the day or month you request through MLS Assist while you are signed in to athenaOne. A supervised history import reads only the patient you selected. Neither action is a server-side nightly backup.

🌙 Optional extension snapshot: from the MLS Assist toolbar, you can schedule a capture of the one exact patient chart already open in signed-in athenaOne. It never walks through every patient. If a stable, verified chart is not open, nothing is read or sent. This requires that computer, Chrome, and your Athena session to remain available.

This nightly backup uses your EMR's official API connection (separate from the Visit tab's "Pull this day", which reads athenaOne through your office computer). How much it can back up depends on the access level your EMR granted — a patient-level connection backs up only that patient until your practice enables practice-wide API access.

Read the full guide

The essentials. You can reopen this anytime from ❓ Help or the 🚀 button.

🎙️ Record a visit → instant note. Open a patient (or “New visit”), press record, and talk through the visit normally. MLS transcribes and writes a structured note. Review, edit, then Sign — your signature block is appended automatically.
👤 Patients. Add patients with “＋ New patient.” Each chart keeps the problem list, meds, allergies, prior visits, and notes. Search by name or DOB up top.
🗓️ Scheduling & booking. Set your hours in 🕘 Availability. Share your booking link; patients pick only open slots and get a confirmation email with a link to confirm or cancel. See everyone on the 🗓️ Check-in board.
🗂 Staff Prep. Open Menu → Staff prep & Athena month pull for explicit day/month schedule pulls and preparation. MLS never starts a hidden Athena pull.
👤 Patient portal. Select the exact patient, then use the active-patient Patient portal control. Review the frozen identity and email before sending an invite.
🧩 MLS Assist (browser extension). Install it to let MLS work with your real EMR (e.g. Athena): read a chart into MLS and prepare the finished note with an exact, visible destination plan. You remain in control of every Athena save or submission. Reload to the latest version at chrome://extensions.
✨ Create your own + 🔗 connectors. Build custom tabs/widgets by describing them, and connect via the FHIR API. All under the tools menu.
❓ Stuck? Hit ❓ Help anytime and ask “where is…” or “how do I…”. Answers are specific to this app.
